title: Dentist Office in a Mall:
content: I had a dream last night that I’m pretty sure was NOT Mall world related but as I was thinking about it early in the morning, still groggy from waking up, it reminded me of a dream I had once. I don’t really remember when I had this dream, I know I wasn’t a child, and it was probably only a couple years or so ago but I was having flashbacks of the main concepts of this dream and I thought about how fitting to Mall World it had been looking back on it. What I remember of the dream, I was actually in a mall. A mall with a huge tree growing in the middle of the food court and trees in some other places around the mall. Giant, beautiful trees of a species I’m not sure, they looked like a mix between a common Oak and an Evergreen tree. Some had fruit growing on it that did not look familiar to me, large apple-like fruit that was purple instead of red. There were birds in some of these trees and they echoed throughout the mall. The Mall was almost empty save for a few shoppers here and there and I remember there was this open lounge area in the middle between some stores that lined each side. Well, it was more of a waiting area. Everything you expect out of a typical waiting area of a dentists office. Except it was all out in the middle of the mall, out in the open, no walls or anything separating the dentist chairs or patients being worked on. It was like those massage vendors you see around the mall. There was even a long fish tank behind a row of waiting chairs. Anyway, the dream itself isn’t that exciting, I was getting dental surgery right in the middle of the mall where everyone can see me and there was no such thing as pain or anesthesia, so the only thing I felt during that dream was embarrassment because my teeth were so bad and anyone could walk over and see it. The dream got worse when my dentist said I needed “special work” and to “go up the escalator to the second floor” to more rooms. I did, and the process repeated. The stations at the top of the escalator were larger. It looked like a food court but instead of restaurants, tables and chairs it was just endless dentist chairs. Same painless dental surgery and even more embarrassment because everyone I know was there watching it happen. It does make sense why I had this dream though, I have the distinct memory of waking up and remembering I had a dentist appointment that day, and I walked out (the real dentist office after my actual appointment, I mean) after having to get two fillings for cavities and half my weeks paycheck gone.
